preview.title: How Depots and Releases Are Organised
preview.summary: Depot reports describe a shared, locally operated workflow with city-specific capacity or operational changes. The release process is described as a gated sequence, with build and deploy details available but the third gate unspecified.

content.text: The depot reports describe a recurring operational routine at each location, alongside city-specific changes in staffing, equipment, capacity or working conditions. The release notes instead describe a staged process: they state that every release passes through three gates, and give details for build and deploy.

Across the city reports, shift leads review loading bays, sorting belts and the returns desk each morning. Drivers collect routes from the dispatch office and scan parcels at the gate; customers can track deliveries, and supervisors prepare weekly delay summaries. The reports therefore present depot work as a location-based operation with recurring checks, dispatch and follow-up.
Staffing increased by six after the spring hiring round.
Closed early twice because of storms.
Added a third sorting belt in April.
Lost two delivery vans to a recall.
Paused night shifts during an ice warning.
Moved the returns desk to the east bay.
Opened a second loading dock on the river side.

Releases are organised around gates and assigned stage ownership. The documented build stage, owned by Alice, compiles the sources and runs unit tests. The deploy stage, owned by Bob, restarts workers one at a time.
City-specific depots with a recurring local operating routine.
Stages or gates within a release process.
Daily operational checks and dispatch, with weekly delay summaries.
Build activities followed by a deploy step that restarts workers one at a time.
Reports record local differences in parcel volumes and operational changes or constraints.
Build is assigned to Alice and deploy to Bob; the notes say there are three gates but detail only two stages.

In short, the depot material emphasizes consistent routines adapted to local conditions, while the release material emphasizes a gated workflow with named owners and specific build and deploy actions. The available release notes do not identify the third gate, so a complete stage-by-stage comparison is not possible.
